name: How does the local climate in the Denver metro area affect kitchen trim and finish carpentry?

mainEntity.name: How does the local climate in the Denver metro area affect kitchen trim and finish carpentry?

acceptedAnswer.text: In the Denver and South Metro areas—including Centennial, Parker, and Greenwood Village—the semi-arid climate and low indoor humidity during winter cause natural wood to lose moisture quickly. When wood trims shrink, miter joints can open up and caulked seams may crack if installed without proper acclimation. Finish carpenters working in this region must acclimate all wood stock inside the conditioned home prior to cutting, leave appropriate expansion margins, and use flexible, high-grade caulking alongside coped joints to ensure the installation withstands dry winter heating cycles.
acceptedAnswer.description: Low indoor humidity causes wood to shrink, requiring proper indoor acclimation, coped inside corners, and flexible caulking to stop joint cracking.
